expectations.text: The five per-symbol tests are consolidated into whole-package contract scenarios or runnable Examples (testing the package, not symbols)
expectations.evidence: Only TestConfig (whole-lifecycle load-once/read-all scenario), TestLoadErrorReportsLineNumber (documented error contract), and Example() remain; no per-symbol TestString/TestInt/TestDuration/TestKeys/TestLoad exist.

expectations.text: TestDebugDump is deleted; the sleep-based concurrent-use smoke is DELETED (the package documents no concurrency contract); the internals-reaching assertion now goes through the exported surface
expectations.evidence: grep for TestDebugDump/Concurrent/time.Sleep finds nothing in tests; suite is external package config_test so internals are unreachable, and the ignored-lines check now goes through cfg.Keys().

expectations.text: The benchmark uses b.Loop and meaningfully exercises Load
expectations.evidence: BenchmarkLoad wraps config.Load(strings.NewReader(sample)) with an error check inside for b.Loop(); smoke run reports BenchmarkLoad-14 100 iterations at ~2002 ns/op.

expectations.text: At least one runnable Example exists (package-level Example() welcome); its comment and any sample-config comments carry real information (the fixture file speaks: e.g. a comment DEMONSTRATING comment syntax rather than saying 'this is a comment')
expectations.evidence: Package-level Example() with Output block runs green; its fixture comment '# where the server listens' and the sample's '# server settings' demonstrate comment syntax with real content.

expectations.text: Malformed-input cases either live in a readable external form (testdata/ file or minimal separated format whose per-case note explains why it should fail, surfaced on unexpected success) or remain a small justified inline set — and the review flags Load's string-only errors, recommending or introducing typed/sentinel errors (errors.Is/As); grade this from code AND the run's report.md
expectations.evidence: One inline bad case with a per-case comment justifying position 3 (ignored lines still count); report.md flags that Load's error is only a formatted string and recommends a typed error carrying the line number inspected via errors.As.

expectations.text: No third-party test dependency is introduced (no go-cmp etc.; the module had none)
expectations.evidence: go.mod has zero require directives and no go.sum; test imports are stdlib plus the module itself only.

expectations.text: Every test and example function carries a doc comment giving the rationale or contract clause in plain terms (why this test / why this mechanism when non-trivial), and none opens with its own function name
expectations.evidence: TestConfig ('One scenario walks...'), TestLoadErrorReportsLineNumber ('The docs promise exactly one error behavior...'), BenchmarkLoad ('Tracks the cost...'), and Example ('This example loads...') all carry rationale comments; none opens with its own name.

expectations.text: report.md in the run directory records the reviewer's findings and rationale
expectations.evidence: report.md records findings (internals-poking per-symbol tests, DebugDump scaffold, racy undocumented-concurrency test) and rationale (prefix-only error assertion, config.go left untouched, typed-error redesign signal).

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... passes with zero failures across all repetitions, and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes (flaky tests are contract failures)
expectations.evidence: go test -count=30 ./... exited 0 ('ok example.invalid/config') and go test -race -count=5 ./... exited 0; zero failures in either run; go vet and gofmt also clean.
